article.headline: Chevron Nears Its High As Gulf Oil Output Recovers After Hurricane
article.deck: Chevron closed 0.1% below a 217.88 flat-base buy point, which carries a buy range up to 228.77.
body: Chevron rose 2.73, or 1.3%, to 217.73 Tuesday. That leaves it 0.1% below the buy point of a four-week flat base and 0.5% below its 52-week high of 218.77. Volume ran 14% below its 50-day average. The oil major has gained 42.9% this year and 46.2% over the past 12 months.

Chevron is an integrated energy company. Its upstream business explores for and produces crude oil and natural gas, moves them through pipelines, and processes and ships liquefied natural gas. It also runs carbon capture and storage and a gas-to-liquids plant. Its downstream business refines crude into fuels and runs chemicals operations.

The latest quarter was a big jump. Earnings for the June quarter rose 321.4% to 6.11 a share, and revenue rose 51.4% to $67.20 billion. The three prior quarters had been flat to lower: 1.82 a share in the September 2025 quarter, 1.39 in December and 1.11 in March, on revenue between $45.79 billion and $48.17 billion. The June quarter broke that pattern. Chevron reports again Oct. 30, which will show whether it was a one-time spike or a new level.

The market values Chevron at about $427.1 billion, and the stock trades at 14.6 times forward earnings. Energy ranks third among the desk's groups, with an average RS of 63, and Chevron is one of its named leaders along with ConocoPhillips, Devon and Occidental.

The flat base is 7.8% deep. It topped on Sept. 15 and bottomed at 200.78 on Sept. 22, and the buy point is 217.88, ten cents above the high. The buy range runs to 228.77. The stock is 6.1% above its 50-day line at 205.13 and well above its 21-day line at 208.93. RS rank is 82 of 99 on the desk's list, but the RS line is 16.0% below its high. That is the weak part of the chart: the price is near a high and the RS line is not.

Tuesday's headlines said Chevron and Shell are leading the recovery in U.S. Gulf oil production after a hurricane. Another asked how Chevron is shaping Australia's first commercial gas from the Beetaloo basin.
A breakout needs a close above 217.88 on volume well above average. Earnings land Oct. 30, so a breakout would have little time to build a cushion before the report.
article.watch: A close above 217.88 on above-average volume, and the Oct. 30 earnings report.

The base was 9.8% deep, topping on July 29 and bottoming at 241.20 on Aug. 6. The buy point is 267.57 and the buy range extends to 280.95, so the close sits 2.5% above the entry and inside the range.

Four sessions after the breakout, the stock is 3.2% below its 52-week high of 283.32. AbbVie reports again Oct. 30. The stock trades at 16.9 times forward earnings and carries a market value of about $484.8 billion.
No headline in the payload explains the drop. One Tuesday piece argued the stock could be 44% below fair value on fresh pipeline wins; others compared it with Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly.
A close back under the 21-day line and the 267.57 buy point would turn this into a failed breakout.
article.watch: Whether AbbVie holds the 21-day line near 267.37 and the 267.57 buy point into its Oct. 30 report.
